title: Growth Creative Operations
description:
TL;DR: Lovable's growth marketing runs on creative. The volume, variety, and quality of concepts we put in front of people, and how fast what we learn from them turns into the next round. Your job is to own that loop end to end, constantly iterating on it to achieve the best results against your KPIs.

Why Lovable?

Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started.

We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.

Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.

What we’re looking for

  • You've run high-volume creative testing on performance marketing and can talk specifically about what you learned, not just what you shipped.

  • You use AI tools daily and have built something with them that other people now depend on. A workflow, an agent, an internal tool, a tagging pipeline.

  • You have opinions about what makes an ad work and can articulate them well.

  • You write well for ads. Briefs, hooks, scripts etc.

  • You're comfortable being wrong in public. A lot of tests lose, and the loop only works if we’re all comfortable with that.

  • You move fast, but balance that with exceptional craft and know where the balance is.

What you’ll do

You'll be the person who decides what we test, why, and what the results mean. Then you'll build the workflows that turn those answers into hundreds of assets a month without losing the taste that made them work in the first place.

  • Own the creative operating system. You run creative ops for performance marketing: intake, briefing, production, QA, launch, and post-mortem. You'll define how the process works and then automate the parts that don't need a human in the loop.

  • Be the creative performance decision maker. When we can produce hundreds of creatives, you’ll be the person to judge what we make more of, what gets killed and what to slightly edit. That means holding the creative standard high, and making sure that creatives generated look Lovable.

  • Build agentic workflows and keep improving them. You'll design pipelines that generate, adapt, and localise creative at volume, with evals to check quality before anything ships. When a workflow breaks, you diagnose it and help rebuild it.

  • Turn performance data, audience insights and product knowledge into concepts. You'll dig into what's actually driving results, hook, format, message, subject, pacing, offer, and separate the signal from the noise a low-spend winner creates.

  • Run brainstorms and briefing. You own the rhythm that takes learnings, customer language, competitor moves, product releases, and additional context, and works with the wider team to turn them into briefs.

  • Push learnings across the company. What wins on paid usually tells us something about the website, lifecycle emails, App Store listings, and organic content. You'll be the one making sure that reaches the relevant people so we become more informed collectively.

About your application

Please submit your application in English. It’s our company language, so you’ll be speaking lots of it if you join.

We treat all candidates equally - if you’re interested, please apply through our careers portal.

title: Product Ops
description:
Our Mission

At Omnea, we’re reinventing how enterprise businesses operate, starting with the most painful parts: procurement – where a single purchase can drag on for months, trigger 50+ emails, and pull in Finance, Legal, Security, and IT just to get something approved.

We’ve raised $75M from Khosla Ventures, Insight Partners, and Accel to change that. Our AI-native platform connects every person, step, and system so buying is fast, safe, and efficient – one place to request, automated approvals and renewals, real-time supplier risk, and complete spend visibility.

The opportunity is massive. Every enterprise on the planet has this problem and nobody has solved it. We’ve 10x’d ARR to double-digit millions in 18 months and are trusted by global enterprises like Spotify, MongoDB, Monzo, and Albertsons. We’re now the 4th fastest growing startup in Europe & the Sunday Times' #1 Best Medium Sized Tech Company To Work for.

Our team previously scaled Tessian (cybersecurity tech, backed by Sequoia, Balderton, Accel, acquired post-Series C), and our team includes ex-founders operators who’ve grown unicorns, shipped world-class products, and executed at the highest levels. You’ll work alongside leaders like Ben, Abs, Sabrina, and Rebe.

Find out more about the team and life at Omnea here.

What we're looking for

This is the first dedicated Product Operations hire at Omnea. You'll report to our VP Product.

You'll live at the intersection of product and AI. You'll build the operational layer a fast-growing product team needs: the tool stack, the launch rhythm, our top-level metrics, early access programmes, the comms.

Treat the product org as your user. Define the problem, build the thing, get people using it, then check whether it made anyone faster. If it didn't, kill it and try something else.

We want a structured operator with low ego and a builder's instinct. You'd rather automate a problem than write a process doc about it. You'll be hands-on — wiring up integrations, writing Claude skills, pulling data, shipping dashboards.

What Can You Expect?

AI enablement for the product team. You'll work out where PMs, designers and engineers are spending time they shouldn't, then build the agents, Claude skills and automations that take it off them: synthesising customer signal from Gong, Slack and support, turning specs into first drafts, generating release notes, assembling reporting. Getting people to use what you build matters as much as building it, so expect to spend real time on adoption and coaching. Hold yourself to whether the team is measurably faster.

The product tool stack. Claude (incl skills), Figma, Linear, Notion, Pylon, Mixpanel, Datadog, Granola, our AI tooling, whatever comes next. You own how it's configured, how it connects and how well it's used. Kill what isn't earning its licence. Run the evaluation when we need something new. Connect them up so nobody's copy-pasting between systems. And structure our sources of truth — roadmap data, decision logs, product knowledge — so agents can read them as well as people can.

Launch and release coordination. The product launch calendar, readiness criteria, and a reliable record of what shipped when. The important part is the join between what we build and how we sell it. Product Marketing owns the narrative and the campaign and marketing release timing; you own the reality underneath it. You’ll know the product inside & out, you’ll ensure that the thing we're announcing has actually shipped, works, is documented for internal teams and customer, and a customer can use it on day one. Nothing goes out before it's ready. Nothing meaningful ships without the market hearing about it.

Early access programmes. Alpha, beta and design partner programmes are how we de-risk what we build and how our best customers get a stake in the roadmap. They run informally today. As we sell to bigger and more demanding enterprises they need proper structure: who gets in, what both sides commit to, how feedback gets captured and routed, and what has to be true before something goes GA. You'll design that and mature it as our customer base does.

Top-level metrics. PMs own the detail for their own areas and should keep owning it. You own the layer above: our North Star and company-level product metrics, the key metric from each team pulled into one picture, kept current and actually looked at. You’ll shape the narrative around the metrics and work with PMs to connect the detail into the company level. You'll bring in the signals from outside product that should be shaping decisions — pipeline and what we're winning on, customer health, how people really use what we've shipped. Board and investor materials should pull from your view rather than getting rebuilt from scratch every quarter.

Product comms, including the roadmap deck. The internal newsletter, release notifications, release tracking. As we ship faster this becomes the difference between a business that's aligned and one that's guessing — Sales, Customer and Marketing should never be surprised by something we've shipped. You'll also own our external-facing roadmap deck, used with prospects and customers and as an internal alignment tool.

Documentation. Integration guides, technical docs and product reference material that get used live in sales cycles and onboarding. You'll keep them accurate as the product grows, you’ll track their adoption and adjust.

How the product team comes together. A team growing this fast needs coherence. You'll run our quarterly or semi-annual product events, and wider R&D events where it makes sense, with a real agenda and a real outcome rather than a day of slides. You'll also own our learning rhythm: lunch and learns, internal teach-ins, and getting good external speakers in from other product orgs.

About You

  • You've spent 2 to 3 years in product operations, product management, business operations, strategy and ops, consulting or a chief-of-staff role, ideally in B2B SaaS. The strongest candidates will have done more than one of those, and will have built the systems they ran rather than inherited them.

  • AI is already how you work. Not something you're planning to get to. You use it instinctively, and more usefully, you know how to design systems that leverage it for other people. You've built agents, automations or internal tools that others adopted and kept using. You can get to a working prototype without waiting for engineering.

  • You're comfortable with data. You can pull it, interrogate it and turn it into something a PM will act on.

  • You're a systems thinker. You know the difference between a process problem and a structural one, and when to optimise versus when to redesign.

  • You write well. You can take a roadmap, a release, or a pile of signals from across the business and make it land with people who didn't build it.

  • You can hold an event with a lot of moving parts and senior people in it, and land it.

  • You have experience in a start up or scale-up environment.

  • You have a track record of top performance, in academia or work or both.

At Omnea, we embrace diversity. To build a product that's loved by everyone, we're best served by a team with all sorts of backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't quite match the full job spec! And regardless of your race, religion, colour, gender, or anything else! If you think you could be a good fit for Omnea, please reach out.

A few things to note:

  • We offer competitive geo-localised benefits, and you can check out our UK Benefits Package here and our US Benefits Package here.

  • We work Tuesdays, Wednesdays & Thursdays in-person at our offices. At this early stage of our company life-cycle it's important to us that we get this together-time, and you can read more about why we believe this is a winning move here

title: People Operations Specialist
description:
At Pencil, we are driving innovation in advertising technology through our state-of-the-art SaaS product, which harnesses Generative AI to redefine content creation. Our mission is to make AI the default in advertising without replacing creative people. To achieve this, we need to make sure that our technology isn’t just in the hands of big brands - we need to try to help small businesses and creative individuals too.

We're looking for someone who loves building automations, agents and workflows, and wants to point that instinct at People Ops. You'll own the data and systems behind our People Ops stack (HiBob, Ashby, Remote), and use that ownership as the foundation for turning slow, manual, multi-tool processes into things that mostly run themselves. This is a role for someone who'd rather ship a working automation this week and improve it next week than spend a month planning the perfect system - someone who gets a genuine kick out of making the unglamorous stuff disappear. You’ll bring expertise, energy, and commercial thinking to help us elevate our People processes.

Key responsibilities:

  • Design, build, and maintain automations, workflows, and AI agents across our People Ops tooling (HiBob, Ashby, Remote) - from a simple triggered workflow to a more sophisticated internal agent - turning multi-step manual processes into things that run themselves.

  • Own the data layer everything else depends on: keep HiBob/Ashby/Remote data clean, resolve integration and schema issues between systems, and treat data integrity as the foundation of what you build, not an afterthought.

  • Run new joiner onboarding end to end, but treat every manual step you touch twice as a candidate for automation, with the goal is to keep making the process faster and lighter-touch, not just execute it reliably.

  • Administer employee lifecycle changes (promotions, transfers, terminations) across systems, and build the guardrails - validation rules, alerts, review steps etc, that catch data errors before they become a downstream mess in payroll or compliance.

  • Process documentation: create and maintain SOPs, checklists, and playbooks for onboarding, offboarding, and systems admin current as processes evolve, so nothing lives only in your head.

  • Partner with relevant stakeholders on anything touching UK employment or compliance judgement calls while you build fluency here. You own the system and the escalation path, and that ownership shifts to you over time.

Your background:

  • You can genuinely build: hands-on with automation/workflow tools (e.g. Zapier, Make, n8n, Retool or similar), and you've actually built or configured AI agents.

  • You've worked with structured data and APIs enough to reason about schemas, integrations, and what breaks when two systems disagree with each other.

  • You're comfortable being the systems administrator of SaaS platforms: owning permissions, workflows, and integrations, ideally across an HRIS/ATS/EOR stack (HiBob, Ashby, Remote) or a comparable set of business systems.

  • You've worked in a high-growth environment, ideally remote and across multiple geographies, and you're comfortable working async across EMEA time zones.

  • Any exposure to People Ops, HR systems, or UK employment practices is a genuine bonus, not a

  • requirement - we're hiring for the builder instinct first, and will coach the domain knowledge.

You’ll Thrive Here If You…

  • You're an Owner. You don't wait to be told the onboarding flow needs fixing, you notice the friction and you just fix it.

  • You're Fast. You'd rather ship a working automation this week and improve it next week than spend a month designing the perfect one.

  • You like Simple. Your default build is the one with the fewest moving parts, not the most impressive one.

  • You find Surprising in the unglamorous stuff. You get a kick out of turning "someone does this by hand every month" into something nobody thinks about again.

  • You're Human, even with agents. You know the systems you're building sit behind someone's first week at a new job, or a colleague's benefits question — you design for that person, not just for the workflow diagram.

KPIs & Success Measures

  • Number and scope of manual People Ops processes automated, and time saved per cycle

  • HiBob / Ashby / Remote data accuracy rate

  • Time to resolve employee systems requests

  • Reduction in error rate flowing into compliance-relevant fields

Benefits:

  • 25 days PTO plus public holidays, although we operate a Flexible Time Off scheme

  • Health insurance / private medical cover

  • Monthly stipend towards wellness, fitness, and learning and development

  • Remote - work from anywhere in your home country

  • Enhanced parental leave policies, whether you become a parent through birth, adoption or surrogacy

  • Access to our Pencil office in The Shard, London for UK employees

  • Flexible working hours

description:
Role: Product Owner – Communication Channels & AI

Location: Manchester

Hours: Monday-Friday 8:45am-5:15pm

Package: £80k OTE

 

As Product Owner - Technical Products, your role is to own and continuously improve PHMG's Technical product portfolio, ensuring Cloud Telephony, AI Receptionist and CCE deliver measurable client value, operational quality and long-term commercial growth. 

You are accountable for translating client needs, technology capability, partner opportunities and commercial priorities into scalable products and service models that strengthen adoption, retention and PHMG's competitive position. 

Through H2 2026, you will lead the evolution of the technical product portfolio by bringing together product performance, platform capability, roadmap execution, client outcomes, commercial discipline, operational readiness and cross-functional alignment into one coherent product improvement agenda. 

 

Key Objectives 

Core Accountability 

  • Own the strategy, design and ongoing performance of Cloud Telephony, AI Receptionist and CCE.
  • Set a clear, prioritised roadmap that balances client value, technical feasibility, commercial return, operational capacity and partner dependency.
  • Ensure Technical products are positioned, sold, onboarded, serviced and renewed in a way that delivers measurable value for clients.
  • Define the product standards, service models and client journeys that CS and Technical Production can execute consistently.
  • Bring clarity to build, buy and partner decisions so product direction is deliberate, commercially disciplined and scalable.

 

Technical Product Strategy & Roadmap 

  • Define the long-term direction for Cloud Telephony, AI Receptionist and CCE, including the sequence of capability, integrations and service-model changes.
  • Prioritise AI Receptionist growth across both horizontal capability and the vertical use cases where PHMG has the strongest right to win.
  • Create a clear approach for CCE in the existing base, reducing under-utilisation and turning technical review, onboarding and value evidence into retention levers.
  • Partner with the Creative Product Owner so the full product set feels coherent to clients and to the teams selling and servicing it.

 

 

Client Experience, Adoption & Value Evidence 

  • Define the client experience for Technical products across onboarding, configuration, in-life usage, renewal and offboarding.
  • Clarify how clients access, configure and understand product value through the portal, including call flows, AI Receptionist behaviour, CCE setup and usage analytics.
  • Ensure CS has the standards, data and language needed to evidence value, drive adoption and manage client expectations confidently.
  • Identify where clients slow, stall or disengage, and build product or service-model interventions that protect retention.

 

Commercial Performance & Partner Discipline 

  • Own the commercial logic of the Technical portfolio, including pricing, CAC, cost-to-serve, gross margin, revenue performance and investment cases.
  • Operationalise the GoTo resell model with clear pricing, service, process and margin controls while protecting the partner relationship.
  • Use data to assess where Technical products create incremental value, where they cannibalise existing activity and where the model needs to change.
  • Make active trade-offs between speed, quality, margin, client experience and platform investment.

 

Operational Delivery & Launch Readiness 

  • Work with Technical Production and Tech to define standards, SLAs, runbooks and support models for each product and release.
  • Ensure new capabilities do not go live until operational readiness, client communications, CS briefings and support routes are clear.
  • Create tight governance for launch decisions, technical dependencies, client escalations, recurring provisioning issues and partner constraints.
  • Keep accountability clear between Product, Tech and Product Operations so issues are solved at the right level rather than absorbed by CS.

 

Insight, Reporting & Continuous Improvement 

  • Maintain a reliable view of product performance across adoption, usage, NPS, retention, revenue, margin, service issues and operational friction.
  • Build structured feedback loops with CS, Client Insights, Sales, Tech and Technical Production to identify product problems worth solving.
  • Turn recurring client or operational issues into permanent product, process, reporting or service-model improvements.
  • Use performance data to make early decisions before product issues become retention, margin or client-experience risks.

 

 

About PHMG:

Established in 1998, PHMG has grown from a renowned Manchester-based business to the world's leading audio branding agency – working with 36,000 clients in 54 countries across the globe. This expansive client list includes household names of the calibre of Samsung, Audi and Adidas, as well as SMEs in every sector of the global market.
